- The Oregon Country was jointly occupied by the United States and British interests from 1818
- The dispute was between the U.S. and what was then British North America (the territories controlled by Britain/United Kingdom)
- The Oregon Treaty of 1846 established the 49th parallel as the boundary
- "United Kingdom" refers to the sovereign state of Britain including England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland
- "Great Britain" refers specifically to England, Scotland, and Wales (the island nations)

1. It provides specific dates (1818-1846) showing the timeline of joint occupation
2. It references the specific treaty (Oregon Treaty of 1846) that resolved the dispute
